Header: Helicoverpa zeae , Heliothis virescens Cotton bollworm, Tobacco budworm

Prevention: Avoid growing cotton in close proximity to alternate host crops, e.g. pigeon pea, sweet potato, tomato
Use of trap count information to determine if
Heliothis sp. will be a serious pest in your area.
If numbers are high, consider planting elsewhere or planting an alternative crop
Monitoring: Eggs - spherical, flattened, 10-15 perpendicular rows of toothed ribs, range from white, cream and dark brown.
Act when 10% of plant terminals examined contain eggs.
Larvae- rows of dark bristled tubercles along back, mature larvae are green, brown or yellow.
Search for young larvae at the base of young bolls.
At post-bloom stage, act if 3 terminals per 100 terminals contain live larvae or when more than 5% bolls are affected.
Look for squares, floral buds or immature bolls that have fallen to the ground and rosetted flowers.
Adults – use pheromone traps to attract male adults (1 trap for every 5 acres) act if you trap more than 7 in one night
Direct Control: Delay use of insecticides as long as possible to allow build-up of natural enemies e.g.
Trichogramma sp., Green lacewing ( Chrysopa sp.) larvae and minute pirate bugs ( Orius insidiosus )
Restrictions: PPE is worn when spraying these chemicals
Bt) at a rate of 1-3 tbs per gallon, 0.5 – 1.5 pints per acre.
Bt when the immature stages of the target pest are feeding.
Bt pest control products have a shorter shelf life than most chemical insecticides and should be stored in a cool, dark place.
Do not apply if there is a risk of rain within 24 hours of application.
Neem oil (Trilogy) emulsion at a rate of 1 tbsp neem oil for 0.25 litre of water and 4 tbsp neem oil for 1 gal. of water
Strictly avoid adding more neem oil than the recommended quantity.
IRAC MoA -1B Thiamethoxam (Actara) at 2.5g per gal. or 26-39g per ac.
